alex: Quick sync — I sketched an approach for eviction apportioning when tenants have mixed QoS. TL;DR: split the eviction budget into SLA buckets and maintain a tiny soft-reserve per-tenant to avoid thrash. Need sanity check on races and correctness corners.
rachel: Curious how this behaves on hotkey migration (tenant spikes moving across nodes). Does the soft-reserve prevent double-evict during handoff?
sam: Soft-reserve helps but only if it's tied to a lease or token. If a tenant moves and both nodes think they own a partial reserve we can still overshoot. Suggest monotonic token + lease epoch check.
alex: Agreed. Sketch config I had in mind: 
```
evict:
  buckets:
    - critical: 30%
    - standard: 60%
    - best-effort: 10%
  soft_reserve_window_ms: 500
```
This keeps the runtime cheap (local) but gives headroom for in-flight reads.
sophie: Observability question: we'll need per-tenant "reserve-used" and "evict-aborted-by-epoch" counters. If we just rely on heuristics we'll blindside SRE during load tests.
devops-bot: Deploy queued: canary/flavor-evict-apportion v0.1 -> staging at 2026-03-22T15:11:00Z :rocket: (owner: alex)
rachel: Another race: tombstones + rapid rehydration. If node A evicts because of budget, node B rehydrates the same prefix and issues a write that expects the prefix to still be canonical. We need a rule: evict cannot create visibility gaps. Maybe evict only clears KV in-memory but keeps a compact tombstone visible to readers until commit epoch.
sam: That implies we need a lightweight demote marker that travels with epoch+token. Pseudocode check: `if token.epoch != lease.epoch: reject_eviction()` — simple and idempotent. Also, prefer to stamp demote markers with a monotonic sequence to avoid double-apply.
alex: Good call. That keeps eviction stateless-ish but still safe. Implementation plan: phase 1 — local buckets + per-tenant reserve + epoch checks (no cross-node coordination). Phase 2 — optional cross-node settlement where nodes reconcile reserve deficits (for Dedicated pools).
sophie: For phase 1 perf tests: I'll run a mixed QoS blast with 10k tps, hotkey migration every 30s. We'll look for "evict-thrash" and "double-evict" alerts. I'll own dashboards. @sophie please add the synthetic to the chaos suite.
sam: API surface: keep it tiny. Don't expose buckets to callers, just provide a best-effort hint endpoint for admission: `/evict/claim?tenant=XXX&want_ms=200`. Runtime returns `granted_ms` and a `claim_token` (token has epoch). If the token is stale the evict path refuses.
rachel: Needs clarification for Dedicated vs Hosted — Dedicated clusters may want deterministic apportioning across nodes. Phase 2 API could be a settlement RPC that shifts unused grant to others. But let's not block phase 1 on that.
alex: Action items: 1) sam prototype claim API + token logic — due EOW. 2) sophie perf + dashboards for chaos. 3) rachel write up a short ops runbook for canary behavior and what to roll back on. I'll put a draft RFC blurb in #eng-runtime docs.
sam: I'll mock token format: `{"tenant":"t1","epoch":42,"seq":1003}` and try a noop-stamped revoke path.
rachel: For canary, prefer 1% traffic on heavy-tenancy clusters first. Watch these signals: evict_granted_rate, evict_reject_epoch, reserve_exhaustion.
alex: Sounds good. If we see low false positives we can widen. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
sophie: +1, will add dashboards and schedule a run.

alex: leaving this thread — will sync tomorrow after sam's prototype results.
